observations.fault_point: worker exits before external marker write
worker writes and closes marker, then exits before terminal frame

experiment.interpretation: Both fault points produce the same host terminal, while the independent effect oracle differs. A failed worker terminal therefore does not establish that an external effect did not occur.

cases.name: cancel at full handler budget
cases.observation: A second request was rejected while all slots were reserved; cancel consumed its terminal, released reservations, and a follow-up request was admitted.

cases.name: timeout at full handler budget
cases.observation: The terminal reported timeout and incomplete handler results; a late handler result was rejected, reservations reached zero, and a follow-up request was admitted.

cases.name: host close at full handler budget
cases.observation: Closing the live host and bus cleared reservations; later handler delivery was rejected as runtime_closing.

cases.name: duplicate handler result
cases.observation: A duplicate injected after worker-frame parsing was not emitted twice; late_frames increased once and reservations reached zero after consumption.

test_runs.command: python -m pytest tests/test_fault_semantics.py tests/test_events.py tests/test_python_host.py tests/test_providers.py tests/test_llm.py -q

limitations: The test matrix covers a live host; it does not simulate abrupt host/runtime death or power loss.
Duplicate-frame injection occurs after worker-frame parsing and before bus delivery; it is not duplicate IPC bytes.
Admission saturation is deterministic but not a concurrent load or throughput stress test.

crash_window_matrix.restart_method: controlled Runtime shutdown followed by a fresh Runtime on the same workspace; no OS process kill or power-loss simulation

cases.name: accepted before host dequeue
cases.observation: A gate held PythonHost.take_batch after bus admission. The request stayed in the in-process mailbox; shutdown and a fresh Runtime did not replay it, and the marker remained absent.

cases.name: complete frame delivered before injected send error
cases.observation: The worker wrote the marker after complete frame delivery. The host then reported cancelled with reason namespace_reset_before_start and namespace_reset=true.
cases.fault_model: Synthetic local OSError raised after the original write_frame returned; this is semantic ambiguity evidence, not a measurement of ordinary socket failure frequency.

cases.name: terminal queued before actor consumption
cases.observation: The worker effect and python.finished terminal were present; an actor gate left the terminal queued with its reservation. Shutdown and a fresh Runtime did not replay it from the Journal.

cases.name: terminal delivery to closed actor mailbox
cases.observation: Closing the LLM mailbox after python.started caused terminal rejection, incremented undelivered_terminals, and delivered agent.error to the UI; no terminal retry occurred.

cases.name: terminal consumed before interrupted provider response
cases.observation: The scripted provider received python.finished in its request after mailbox consumption. Shutdown while the provider was blocked and a fresh Runtime did not restore the in-memory transcript.

test_runs.command: python -m pytest tests/test_fault_semantics.py tests/test_events.py tests/test_python_host.py tests/test_providers.py tests/test_llm.py -q

limitations: These are controlled in-process gates and Runtime restarts, not abrupt OS process termination or power loss.
The IPC case injects an error after full frame delivery and does not characterize native socket exception behavior.
The tests do not measure concurrent mailbox stress, real remote effects, model quality, provider latency, or token cost.
The original worker-process effect oracle is not a power-loss or storage-failure experiment; the separate abrupt-process probes cover only two gated fault points.
The marker file is not a network service and does not model remote consistency or idempotency.
The original live-host no-replay window is 150 ms; subprocess restart checks separately cover two crash points.
No real-model performance or task-quality claim is measured; the scripted ablation is mechanism-only.

abrupt_process_recovery.relevant_suite_result: Initial combined run: 66 passed, 1 failed because test_python_environment_tool_runs_before_smoke_test exceeded wait_until_idle(8); isolated retry passed, and the combined rerun passed 67.
methodology: Each case launches a child OS process running Runtime and PythonHost against the fixture workspace and shared SQLite Journal.
Sentinel file reports session ID, accepted request ID, Python worker PID, marker state, queued mailbox count, and flushed Journal rows.
Case A holds python.requested before PythonHost.take_batch dequeue; case B holds the LLM actor before consumption after the worker writes the marker and python.finished is offered.
On Windows, the parent uses taskkill /T /F; a recorded worker PID fallback runs only if tree termination failed while the parent was live. POSIX children use a dedicated process group.
The restart uses a new session and does not emit either old request or terminal; marker state remains absent in case A and present in case B.
limitations: Journal flush occurs before OS-process termination; this does not test loss during SQLite/WAL writes or power loss.
Short sentinel polling and bounded restart settling are used; barriers are deterministic at both fault points.
The marker is a local file oracle, not a remote effect or consistency test.
A scripted backend is used; provider state and model recovery are not tested.
Windows process-tree termination is validated only on this environment.
abrupt_process_recovery.worker_cleanup_check: On Windows, a successful taskkill /T /F is treated as sufficient and is not followed by a stale-PID kill; worker PID fallback is attempted only when tree termination fails while the Runtime parent was live. POSIX uses a dedicated process group. No nervipulsa.python_worker process remained after the final targeted test.
